_about: Body Scout. `official` (sourced, one link per number) and `research` (judgement calls with their why and evidence) are written by hand. `reach`, `segments`, `build`, `movement`, `flexibility` and `game` are derived from them by datasets/players/tools/build_bodies.py: do not edit those by hand, change `research` and run the tool. A block marked "estimate": true is an estimate in every number, by the method it states. Method and references: datasets/players/BODY_SOURCES.md.
name: Novak Djokovic

official.how: The ATP Tour profile's own data (HeightCm, WeightKg, BirthDate, PlayHand, BackHand), read from the JSON the profile page loads.

armSpanRatio.why: the traditional ratio for men (1.03); nothing in his look says longer or shorter arms
armSpanRatio.searched: No published wingspan found (searched Nov 11, 2026; only unsourced fan-site guesses).

legShift.why: standard leg share: no evidence of an unusually long- or short-legged build

build.massSits: evenly spread; long, lean muscle and a narrow waist
build.typeWhy: appearance.json calls his build lean and flexible with a very lean torso; the ATP's 82 kg gives BMI 23.2, which on its own would read athletic. Drawn lean.

movement.why: The highest speed Tennis Australia's tracking saw from any man (36.02 km/h) and the tour's reference for sliding defence; then slowed for age (39).
movement.slides: Open-stance slides into near-splits on every surface, hard courts included; he warns that extreme slides need strong, flexible ankles.

evidence.claim: Djokovic 36.02 km/h, the highest top speed of the 12 men listed

published.what: highest speed seen in a match
published.note: Tennis Australia Game Insight Group, three Australian Opens, runs of 3 m or more (tennis.com, Nov 29 2016). A speed seen in matches, not a sprint test, and the method was not published: recorded, not used as his top speed.

Tennis Australia Game Insight Group, three Australian Opens, runs of 3 m or more (tennis.com, Nov 29 2016). A speed seen in matches, not a sprint test, and the method was not published: recorded, not used as his top speed.

flexibility.why: 'I always have worked a lot on my flexibility, since a young age'; 'known for his elasticity'; filmed doing the splits. Top of the scale; no goniometer numbers published
flexibility.spreadWhy: Near a full split: he is filmed pulling the splits, and slides into them in matches.

evidence.claim: 'I always have worked a lot on my flexibility, since a young age. I was taught this was extremely important because that's going to give me longevity.' (Wimbledon 2023); the article calls him 'known for his elasticity'
headline: 'Watch 6'2" Tennis Star Novak Djokovic Pull the Splits With Belgian Gymnasts'
sliding on hard courts: ankle flexibility matters, and Djokovic warns players with fragile ankles to be careful with extreme slides

reach.method: no published wingspan found: arm span = 1.030 x height. the traditional ratio for men (1.03); nothing in his look says longer or shorter arms
reach.standingReachHow: flat-footed, fingertips overhead: shoulder height + arm + 3% of height for the raised shoulder girdle (estimate)
reach.racketReachHow: body centre line to the racket's sweet spot, arm straight out at shoulder height, no lean or step: half the shoulder-joint spacing + upper arm + forearm + 0.50 m (wrist to sweet spot of a 68.6 cm racket). Estimate.
reach.overheadRacketReachHow: sweet spot height with the arm straight up, feet flat (a serve adds the jump). Estimate.

segments.method: standard ratios x his sourced height (Drillis & Contini via Winter; widths as in BODY_SOURCES.md), moved only by research.legShift, research.armSpanRatio and research.build.mul. Not measured on him.

check.what: head+neck + trunk + thigh + shin + foot height must equal his height (within 1 cm); shoulder-joint spacing + 2 x (upper arm + forearm + hand) must equal his arm span

build.bmiHow: weight / height^2 from the official numbers
build.typeHow: appearance.json calls his build lean and flexible with a very lean torso; the ATP's 82 kg gives BMI 23.2, which on its own would read athletic. Drawn lean.
build.massSits: evenly spread; long, lean muscle and a narrow waist

proportions.method: fractions of his height, seen from the front. Widths: Drillis & Contini outer widths; thickness baselines are estimates for an average tour build, scaled by sqrt(BMI / 23.25) and by research.build.mul (the features the Appearance Scout and the video notes call out).

movement.method: no per-player tracking speeds are published for most of the tour, so: the game's own body formula (top = 6.6 x sqrt(h) / w^0.25, accel = 8.6 / w / sqrt(h), h = height / 1.85, w = weight / 75; its 6.6 m/s matches the ATP's 23.58 km/h maximum speed for men's tennis) x a small rating from the evidence below x age (after 30: -0.6% top speed and -0.8% first step per year; legends are modelled at their prime).

ratings.why: The highest speed Tennis Australia's tracking saw from any man (36.02 km/h) and the tour's reference for sliding defence; then slowed for age (39).

movement.changeOfDirectionHow: 1 = average tour player: sqrt(80.8 kg / his weight) x rating x age (a lighter body stops and restarts faster)
movement.slides: Open-stance slides into near-splits on every surface, hard courts included; he warns that extreme slides need strong, flexible ankles.

published.note: Tennis Australia Game Insight Group, three Australian Opens, runs of 3 m or more (tennis.com, Nov 29 2016). A speed seen in matches, not a sprint test, and the method was not published: recorded, not used as his top speed.

why.armSpanM: estimate: 1.030 x height, the traditional ratio for men (1.03); nothing in his look says longer or shorter arms
why.legLengthM: hip joint to floor: (0.530) x height (Drillis & Contini)
why.shoulderW: bone width acromion to acromion: 0.235 x height
why.hipW: outer hip width: 0.191 x height, scaled by build
why.shoulderJointW: shoulder joint centres: shoulderW minus ~3 cm a side (for the skeleton)
why.hipJointW: hip joint centres: 0.095 x height (for the skeleton: the legs hang from here, not from the hip's outer edge)
why.reachM: body centre to sweet spot, arm straight out, standing still; a lean or a step adds to it
why.overheadReachM: sweet spot height with the arm straight up, feet flat (serve contact before the jump)
why.topSpeed: m/s, estimate: body formula x mover 1.04 x age 0.946. The highest speed Tennis Australia's tracking saw from any man (36.02 km/h) and the tour's reference for sliding defence; then slowed for age (39).
why.accel: m/s^2, estimate: body formula x first step 1.04 x age 0.928
why.cod: 1 = average: sqrt(80.8 / weight) x 1.12 x age 0.928
why.flex: 'I always have worked a lot on my flexibility, since a young age'; 'known for his elasticity'; filmed doing the splits. Top of the scale; no goniometer numbers published
why.splitDepth: share of his leg length the hips drop in his widest stance: 1 - cos(165 deg / 2)
